summary: This bill directs the Department of Energy to establish a research and development program for next-generation geothermal systems, including closed-loop and supercritical geothermal technologies, and requires the U.S. Geological Survey to regularly update its geothermal resource assessment to include these advanced systems.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $150,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for next-generation geothermal research and development, which represents a clear increase in government spending for this specific area.

The bill focuses entirely on promoting and developing next-generation geothermal energy systems, which are a form of renewable energy. This directly supports environmental protection by advancing clean energy technologies.

The bill authorizes $150 million annually for FY2027–2031 for next-generation geothermal R&D programs within the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy. This constitutes new directed federal spending that would increase outlays (and thus the deficit, absent offsets), though the spending is incidental to the bill’s core purpose of advancing geothermal energy technology.
